threat_model.model: compromised-host (project default): attacker controls a host and may send arbitrary packets, but cannot reconfigure the control plane
threat_model.reason: Fixture. The point of the test is that the threshold is CONTROL-PLANE supplied and therefore NOT attacker-chosen, which is what makes pinning it sound.

assume.ref: cp_action_param_tna fixture: the deployed controller installs threshold = 20
assume.reason: Without this the synthesized action argument is free-symbolic, so the solver picks 0, the sink flips on the first packet, and the emitted test is a single-send false positive that cannot reproduce on hardware. Pinning it both constrains the emitted entry and gives driveRegisterPhase2 a value to solve k against. 20 is above the 16-packet boundary where the emitter switches from literal tamper_only blocks to a repeat_count block, so the test also covers that path.
